objective: Lossless reduction of candidate space before complete hashing; Q-to-k compression and difficulty scaling are central.
requirements: Never discard a valid candidate in the claimed domain.
Retain candidates when a solver times out or a proof is incomplete.
Freeze exclusions before computing reference answers.
Count complete hashes to first success on retained candidates and the same ordering without pruning.
Report exhausted no-hit domains separately; do not invent a finite time to success.
Measure how retained size and verification attempts change with target difficulty, word width, rounds and unknown input bits.
Account for symbolic constraint work and dictionary/model construction separately.
Use disjoint training and evaluation headers for probability ranking.
Every result must state whether it is added to production miner code, research only, rejected or incomplete.
A toy theorem cannot be treated as a Bitcoin SHA256d theorem without a validated connection.
